slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description: Curb ramps allow people to transition from the sidewalk to the street. They should exist at all crossable intersections.

slide-2.title: Driveway
slide-2.description: Driveways are not curb ramps. They are designed for vehicles and not pedestrians. Driveways should not be labeled as Curb Ramps.

slide-3.title: Garage
slide-3.description: Driveways to garages are not curb ramps. Driveways should not be labeled as Curb Ramps.

slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description: Sidewalk intersections should have curb ramps—ideally two per corner. If a corner has a sidewalk but does not have a curb ramp, place the Missing Curb Ramp label where you think a curb ramp should exist.

slide-2.title: Residential walkways
slide-2.description: Residential walkways should not be labeled as Missing Curb Ramps.

slide-3.title: Not on pedestrian path
slide-3.description: Curb ramps are not needed at paths not intended for pedestrians to pass.

slide-4.title: $t(common:no-sidewalk)
slide-4.description: For corners with no sidewalks, use the No Sidewalk label rather than a Missing Curb Ramp label.

slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description:
Obstacles are barriers that impede pedestrian pathways for people using wheelchairs, walkers, or other mobility aids.

Not all fire hydrants, poles, and signs are obstacles—only those that clearly obstruct pedestrian paths.

slide-2.title: Ample space to maneuver around
slide-2.description: The motorcycle is parked on the side; there is ample space for pedestrians on the remaining space of the sidewalk.

slide-3.title: Obstacle not on sidewalk
slide-3.description:
This traffic cone is not on a pedestrian pathway so it should not be marked as an Obstacle.

Only mark obstacles on sidewalks, crosswalks, and other pedestrian pathways.

slide-4.title: Moving object
slide-4.description: The car seems to be moving in the image and should not be labeled as an Obstacle.

slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description: If something on the sidewalk or crosswalk surface would make it uncomfortable or impossible to cross, it should be labeled as a Surface Problem.

slide-2.title: Normal sidewalk tiles
slide-2.description: Normal sidewalk tiles (without gaps, cracks or bumps) are not surface problems.

slide-3.title: Not on pedestrian path
slide-3.description:
This gravel is not on a pedestrian pathway so it should not be marked as a Surface Problem.

Only mark surface problems on sidewalks, crosswalks, and other pedestrian pathways.

slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description: If a street side does not have a sidewalk, please mark it with a No Sidewalk label.

slide-2.title: Median
slide-2.description: A median that separates two directions of a traffic and is not intended for pedestrians should not be labeled as No Sidewalk.

slide-3.title: Pavement
slide-3.description: There is a sidewalk here. It should not be marked as No Sidewalk.

slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description:
A crosswalk is a legally defined space to cross a road.

Crosswalks are often indicated by parallel dashed lines.

slide-2.title: No visual indicator
slide-2.description: Crossings with no visual indicator should not be labeled as Marked Crosswalks.

slide-3.title: Stop line
slide-3.description: Stop lines for cars should not be labeled as Marked Crosswalks.

slide-4.title: Speed bump
slide-4.description: Speed bumps should not be labeled as Marked Crosswalks.

slide-1.title: {{- labelType}}
slide-1.description:
A pedestrian signal indicates when pedestrians can cross the street and provides time for them to do so safely.

Some pedestrian signals are activated by a pedestrian push button at waist height.

slide-2.title: Signage
slide-2.description: This sign does not indicate when pedestrians can cross the street.

slide-3.title: Pole
slide-3.description: This pole does not show traffic signals to pedestrians.

slide-4.title: Traffic light for vehicles
slide-4.description: This traffic light is only for vehicles, not for pedestrians.

wrong-type.text: This is the wrong label type
wrong-type.tooltip: Something is here, but it should be marked with a different label type
wrong-type.tooltip-curb-ramp: Sometimes a missing curb ramp is accidentally mislabeled as a curb ramp
wrong-type.tooltip-no-curb-ramp: Sometimes a curb ramp is mislabeled as a missing ramp, often because it's missing a tactile warning
wrong-type.tooltip-obstacle: Grass and debris like leaves should be marked with a Surface Problem label
wrong-type.tooltip-surface-problem: Gravel or grass are not considered a sidewalk, and should be marked with a No Sidewalk label
wrong-type.tooltip-no-sidewalk: Surface problems or obstacles may be mistakenly labeled as No Sidewalk

driveway-transition.text: This is a sidewalk to driveway transition
driveway-transition.tooltip: Sidewalk to driveway transitions are not curb ramps unless a dedicated ramp has been added

unsafe-crossing.text: It is not safe to cross here
unsafe-crossing.tooltip: Pedestrians are not meant to cross at this spot, so no curb ramp is expected

not-pedestrian-path.text: This is not on a pedestrian path
not-pedestrian-path.tooltip-obstacle: If there is no sidewalk or the object is not on the part of the sidewalk meant for pedestrians, like in the image below, an Obstacle label is not needed
not-pedestrian-path.tooltip-surface-problem: If a surface problem is not on a path meant for pedestrians, it should not be labeled as a surface problem

ample-space.text: There is ample space to avoid this object
ample-space.tooltip: On very wide sidewalks, easily avoidable objects should not be labeled as obstacles

no-visible-crosswalk.text: There is no visible crosswalk here

stop-line.text: This is a stop line for cars

vehicle-signal-only.text: This is only a traffic light for vehicles

sign-no-light.text: This is a sign with no light to indicate safe crossing

pole-no-signal.text: This is a pole with no pedestrian signal or button

better-image.tooltip: This could be because the image is blurry, what's being labeled is too far away, or a different angle is needed

placement-incorrect.tooltip: Sometimes what's being labeled is visible but the label appears far away from it

ramp-required-unsure.text: Not sure if a curb ramp is required
ramp-required-unsure.tooltip-curb-ramp: Some alleyways or commercial driveways require ramps due to height differences, others do not. Sometimes it's not clear if a seam between a sidewalk requires a ramp or tactile surface indicator.
ramp-required-unsure.tooltip-no-curb-ramp: It may be unclear whether pedestrians should be able to cross at an intersection with a busier road

space-to-avoid-unsure.text: There might be enough space to avoid the object
space-to-avoid-unsure.tooltip: The width of the sidewalk may be difficult to judge from a picture

too-minor-unsure.text: Might be too minor to label
too-minor-unsure.tooltip: It may be unclear whether an issue like grass between sidewalk blocks needs to be labeled

sidewalk-needed-unsure.text: Not sure if there should be a sidewalk here
sidewalk-needed-unsure.tooltip: Sometimes more context is necessary, and it's hard to determine if a sidewalk is necessary from just one image

label-type-picker.change-type-hint: Tags that don't fit the new type are removed. A rating carries over only between types rated the same way.
